content:
Title: WP Responsive Images plugin <=1.0 unauthenticated path traversal via 'src' parameter
CVE: CVE-2026-1557
Vendor: stuartbates
Products: WP Responsive Images
CVSS: 7.5 CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
Severity: High (CVSS 7.5)
Vulnerability type: Path Traversal (CWE-22)
Affected products:
- WP Responsive Images (WordPress plugin)
Affected versions:
- <=1.0
Summary: Path traversal vulnerability in the WP Responsive Images WordPress plugin allowing unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files on the server via the 'src' parameter passed to image_handler.php. Affects all versions up to and including 1.0.
Root cause: Improper sanitization of the 'src' query parameter in image_handler.php allows directory traversal sequences (../) to escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files.
Attack requirements:
- Target must run WordPress with the WP Responsive Images plugin installed and active
- Vulnerable endpoint /wp-content/plugins/wp-responsive-images/image_handler.php must be reachable
- No authentication required (unauthenticated attack)
Impact:
- Arbitrary file read by unauthenticated remote attackers
- Potential disclosure of sensitive files (e.g., wp-config.php containing database credentials)
- Confidentiality breach
Evidence:
- CONFIRMED: CVE-2026-1557 describes a path traversal in WP Responsive Images plugin <=1.0 via the 'src' parameter, allowing unauthenticated arbitrary file read (CWE-22, CVSS 7.5)
- CONFIRMED: Vendor/product is the WP Responsive Images WordPress plugin by stuartbates
- CONFIRMED: The vulnerable endpoint is image_handler.php at /wp-content/plugins/wp-responsive-images/image_handler.php, as documented in CrowdSec vpatch rule and Nuclei template
- CONFIRMED: Attack is unauthenticated (no credentials required)
- CONFIRMED: A Nuclei detection template has been published and merged (projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates PR #15592, merged Mar 18 2026), constituting a public PoC/detection artifact
- CONFIRMED: A CrowdSec virtual patching rule (vpatch-CVE-2026-1557) has been merged (crowdsecurity/hub PR #1749, merged Apr 1 2026), matching requests to image_handler.php with '../' in the 'src' argument
- SECONDARY: Watch evidence indicates the observed assets (dellnetworkingvr.dell.com, dellservervr.dell.com, hiringlab.indeed.com, indeedflex.com) are associated with programs (dell, indeed) and use WordPress technology, but no evidence shows these specific assets are running the WP Responsive Images plugin
- NOT OBSERVED: No evidence in the supplied material shows active exploitation of this CVE in the wild; CrowdSec/Nuclei artifacts are defensive detection tools, not proof of exploitation
- UNKNOWN: Whether a patched version exists beyond 1.0; the CVE states 'all versions up to, and including, 1.0' but does not specify a fix version
- NOT OBSERVED: No vendor advisory or patch details were provided beyond the WordPress plugin source code links
Public exploit: True
References:
- https://plugins.trac.wordpress.org/browser/wp-responsive-images/tags/1.0/image_handler.php#L28
- https://plugins.trac.wordpress.org/browser/wp-responsive-images/tags/1.0/SBOutputFile.php#L33
- https://plugins.trac.wordpress.org/browser/wp-responsive-images/tags/1.0/WPResponsiveImages.php#L265
- https://www.wordfence.com/threat-intel/vulnerabilities/id/22c6f81b-d456-44b9-ba6c-8b207a9ee6e1?source=cve
- https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates/pull/15592
- https://github.com/crowdsecurity/hub/pull/1749
